candidates.title: Store as public cooling infrastructure
candidates.shift: Cities are formally designating buildings, potentially including retail, as official 'cool spaces' during heatwaves, turning private commercial space into public climate infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could push retailers into a quasi-utility role during extreme heat, raising new liability, staffing and operations questions — strange because a store becomes a public shelter by policy.
candidates.evidence: London's 'Cool Spaces' scheme cited as a policy response to rising heatwave frequency/intensity in Regional Environmental Change study.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from private commercial space to quasi-public climate refuge, driven by heatwave frequency; if it spreads, retailers would need new operating protocols, insurance categories, and design standards for extreme-heat duty.
candidates.author: Freya Connor, Anna E. Goodden, James J. Porter

candidates.title: Missing standard for real transport-carbon accounting in construction
candidates.shift: Construction material supply chains lack verified, dynamic carbon data for site-transport (EN Module A4), relying instead on static assumptions.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence signal: a dynamic-carbon-accounting standard doesn't yet exist, which will matter as embodied-carbon regulations tighten on new retail construction.
candidates.evidence: Paper flags EN Module A4 'still often calculated with static assumptions rather than verified data.'
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from static, compliance-driven carbon reporting toward dynamic, logistics-based accounting; if adopted, developers/contractors would need live freight-tracking feeding carbon disclosures for every new store build.
candidates.author: Tomo Cerovsek, Igor Jakomin

candidates.title: Houston's opt-out zoning as a stealth density model
candidates.shift: Houston achieved gradual densification since the 1990s by letting neighborhoods selectively opt out of citywide zoning reforms rather than mandating uniform change.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: a replicable 'voluntary densification' playbook that could reshape where retail real estate gets built in sprawl cities; partly known already, leaning Trend.
candidates.evidence: Reported gentle density shift attributed to a neighborhood opt-out provision in citywide reform.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from top-down zoning mandates to opt-in/opt-out incrementalism, driven by political resistance to blanket upzoning; if it spreads, retail developers could see uneven but accelerating infill opportunities in sprawl-belt metros.

candidates.title: Shoppers start trusting agents to buy for them
candidates.shift: Consumer data shows rising comfort letting AI agents make autonomous purchases on their behalf.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: already-covered trend; the deeper stake is checkout/fulfillment infrastructure and store layout for agent-triggered orders — included as Trend for context.
candidates.evidence: Retail Dive reports shoppers 'trusting AI to buy items.'
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from human browsing/purchase toward agent-initiated transactions; if widespread, physical stores may need fulfillment/pickup infrastructure optimized for agent orders rather than in-store browsing.
candidates.author: Tatiana Walk-Morris

candidates.title: Big-box sporting goods normalizes gig last-mile
candidates.shift: Academy Sports partners with Instacart for same-day delivery, extending the gig-delivery model beyond grocery into bulky specialty retail categories.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative Trend: normalizes store-as-microfulfillment-node for non-grocery goods; stake is in-store pick/pack labor and curbside design for bulky items.
candidates.evidence: Retail Dive: Academy Sports 'partnered' with Instacart for same-day delivery.
candidates.initial_analysis: Continuation of stores-as-fulfillment-centers, driven by gig platforms expanding categories; stores need redesigned back-of-house picking zones and curbside pickup even for bulky sporting goods.
candidates.author: Tatiana Walk-Morris

candidates.title: DTC apparel brand bets on physical expansion abroad
candidates.shift: Fabletics plans to triple its international store footprint, countering the e-comm-first narrative for digitally-native brands.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative Trend, counter-narrative to 'retail apocalypse'; worth watching store format choices in new geographies as a real-estate signal.
candidates.evidence: Retail Dive: Fabletics 'opening 45 new stores over the next year' internationally.
candidates.initial_analysis: Represents a continued DTC-to-physical pivot; if sustained, signals appetite for new store formats in non-US markets, relevant to international site selection.
candidates.author: Lara Ewen

candidates.title: Tariff refunds quietly padding retail margins
candidates.shift: A department store's profit growth is driven by tariff refunds rather than sales growth, masking weak underlying demand.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: trade-policy volatility becoming a hidden lever in retail profitability, potentially skewing store investment decisions independent of consumer demand.
candidates.evidence: Retail Dive: 'Sales barely rose, tariff refunds padded... profit' for Dillard's.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from organic growth to policy-driven earnings; if a pattern, retail capex/store-investment decisions could become more exposed to trade-policy cycles than actual demand.
candidates.author: Daphne Howland

candidates.title: Generic 'AI modernization' as retail cost play
candidates.shift: Footwear retailer signs an AI tech deal aimed at modernizing back-end IT systems and cutting costs.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative Hype: vague enterprise-AI-for-efficiency story, likely backend not store-facing; included as baseline comparison against more concrete physical-AI signals.
candidates.evidence: Retail Dive: Crocs deal is to 'modernize its core business and IT systems... reduce costs.'
candidates.initial_analysis: Generic enterprise AI adoption; unlikely alone to change physical store operations, but flags cost pressure driving broad AI rollout across retail IT stacks.
candidates.author: Tatiana Walk-Morris
